questions.subject: English(11)
questions.question:
11. Read the passage and answer the question.
The Sami are an indigenous people living in the northern parts of Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Russia's Kola Peninsula. Originally, the Sami religion was animistic; that is, for them, nature and natural objects had a conscious life, a spirit. Therefore, one was expected to move quietly in the wilderness and avoid making a disturbance out of courtesy to these spirits. Genghis Khan is said to have declared that the Sami were one people he would never try to fight again. Because the Sami were not warriors and did not believe in war, they simply disappeared in times of conflict. They were known as "peaceful retreaters."
The closest meaning of the underlined word animistic, as it is used in the passage, is—
options: The irrational belief in supernatural beings.
The belief that animals and plants have souls.
The belief that animals are gods.
The primitive belief that people can be reincarnated as animals.
